products.name: TESK
products.blurb: An implementation of the GA4GH Task Execution Service (TES) API that runs containerized tasks on any Kubernetes cluster.
products.description: TESK is a task execution engine based on the GA4GH TES standard that runs on Kubernetes. It exposes the TES endpoints, validates incoming task requests and translates them into Kubernetes batch jobs, so tasks run on any standard Kubernetes cluster. It can also stage task inputs and outputs and integrate with workflow managers.
features: Implements the GA4GH Task Execution Service (TES) API
Translates TES tasks into Kubernetes batch jobs
Designed to support any Kubernetes cluster
Handles task inputs and outputs using temporary persistent volume claims (PVCs) as scratch space
Integrates with workflow managers via an FTP account or an accessible PVC
Each task gets its own taskmaster, PVC and executor pods; only the API pod is shared across tasks
howItWorks: The API pod (Tomcat web server) receives and validates TES requests and turns them into Kubernetes jobs.
The API pod creates a taskmaster pod for each task.
The taskmaster starts a filer pod that creates a PVC as scratch space and downloads input files into the locations given in the TES request.
The taskmaster runs the executors as pods, one after the other.
The filer runs once more to push outputs to remote locations; then the PVC is scrubbed and deleted and the task completes.
requirements: A working Kubernetes cluster, version 1.9 or later
A default storage class supporting RWO mode (needed for tasks with I/O)
An FTP account or an accessible PVC (only for workflow-manager integration)

products.name: proTES
products.blurb: A GA4GH TES gateway that injects configurable middleware into task requests before forwarding them to independent TES nodes.
products.description: proTES is a scalable GA4GH TES API gateway that provides centralized features to a federated network of independently operated TES instances. When a TES request arrives, proTES applies the configured middlewares and then forwards it to a suitable TES instance. It can act as a compatibility layer, a load balancer, a public entry point to an enclave of compute nodes, or a way to collect telemetry. A plugin system makes it easy to write middlewares for access control, request/response processing or validation, and for choosing endpoints based on data-use restrictions and client preferences.
features: Flexible middleware injection through a plugin system
Federates containerized workloads across on-premise, hybrid and multi-cloud TES nodes
Built-in load balancing plugin (pro_tes.middleware.task_distribution.random) that distributes tasks randomly across TES endpoints
Built-in 'bring compute to the data' plugin (pro_tes.middleware.task_distribution.distance) that minimizes how far input data travels
OAuth2 bearer-token authorization out of the box
Declarative YAML configuration, based on the FOCA microservice archetype
Asynchronous tracking of forwarded tasks via RabbitMQ and scalable Celery workers
Helm chart for production and Docker Compose for development
quickStart: Open the Swagger UI at http://localhost:8080/ga4gh/tes/v1/ui
products.status: Beta; the API may change without notice

products.name: Cloud Registry
products.tagline: GA4GH Service Registry for the ELIXIR Cloud
products.blurb: An implementation of the GA4GH Service Registry API for registering and discovering GA4GH-compliant services in a federated cloud network.
products.description: Cloud Registry implements the GA4GH Service Registry API for the ELIXIR Cloud. Service entries comply with the ExternalService schema defined by the GA4GH Service Registry specification. Once deployed, the API is served under /ga4gh/registry/v1/ with an interactive Swagger UI at /ga4gh/registry/v1/ui, and it can be probed with simple HTTP calls, for example GET /services.
audience: Developers building on GA4GH service discovery
features: Implements the GA4GH Service Registry API
Service entries follow the GA4GH ExternalService schema
Interactive Swagger UI for exploring the API
Docker Compose deployment for development and testing
Helm chart for cloud-native deployments
Developer API documentation hosted on ReadTheDocs
products.status: Beta; the API may change without notice

products.name: Cloud Components
products.tagline: The component library for federated cloud services
products.blurb: Modular, customizable and extensible web components for building interfaces that interact with cloud infrastructure.
products.description: ELIXIR Cloud Components (ECC) is a library of web components for interacting with cloud infrastructure. Because they are standard web components, they are framework-agnostic and can be dropped into React, Vue, vanilla HTML or any other front-end stack. Components can be restyled to match your brand and extended with your own.
audience: Front-end developers building cloud service UIs
features: Built as web components, so they work in React, Vue, vanilla HTML and other frameworks
Modular and extensible, with documented guidance for making your own components
Themeable: brand color, corner radius, depth, density, sizing, font size and motion are configurable
Client components for GA4GH services, for example a WES runs component (@elixir-cloud/wes)

products.name: Poiesis
products.blurb: A cloud-native GA4GH Task Execution Service (TES) v1.1.0 implementation for Kubernetes.
products.description: Poiesis is a cloud-native implementation of the GA4GH Task Execution Service (TES) v1.1.0, designed for Kubernetes. Like TESK and Funnel it exposes a standards-compliant TES API for running containerized workloads, with an architecture that emphasizes stateless execution, strong authentication and Kubernetes-native operations.
audience: Admins deploying a TES endpoint on Kubernetes
Node operators joining the TES network
features: Implements GA4GH TES v1.1.0
Kubernetes-native task execution
Stateless execution design
Built-in authentication

products.name: Pubgrade
products.blurb: A decoupled publish-subscribe CI/CD service that builds images and notifies subscribed deployments, which update themselves through Pubgrade-Sidecar.
products.description: Pubgrade (Publish-Upgrade) is a decoupled, publish-subscribe-based continuous integration and delivery service. Developers register a Git repository; Pubgrade builds and publishes images and notifies subscribed deployments, which decide autonomously what to do with an update. Pubgrade-Sidecar is co-deployed next to a subscribed service and applies those updates in the cluster. Pubgrade can optionally link to the ELIXIR Cloud Service Registry.
audience: Node operators who want deployments to update themselves
features: Register Git repositories
Create and publish image builds
Register subscriptions per branch or tag
Notify subscribers on new builds
Pubgrade-Sidecar updates the subscribed Kubernetes deployment

relatedRepos.description: Co-deployed next to a subscribed service; receives Pubgrade notifications and updates the deployment's image

products.name: GA4GH SDK & CLI
products.tagline: One SDK and CLI for GA4GH API services
products.blurb: A generic Rust SDK and command-line client for GA4GH API services such as TES and WES.
products.description: The GA4GH SDK is a generic software development kit and CLI for GA4GH API services, written in Rust. Its models are generated from the services' OpenAPI specifications, so it can be extended to further GA4GH or custom OpenAPI-backed services. It is tested against Funnel (TES) and the GA4GH Starter Kit WES.
audience: Developers building clients for GA4GH services
Users scripting TES and WES from the command line
features: Generic SDK and CLI for GA4GH APIs
Models auto-generated from OpenAPI specifications
Tested against TES (Funnel) and WES (Starter Kit) servers

products.name: Conquest
products.tagline: WES control plane for Nextflow, WDL and Snakemake
products.blurb: A GA4GH Workflow Execution Service that runs Nextflow, WDL and Snakemake pipelines on Kubernetes, with S3 as the data plane.
products.description: Conquest implements a GA4GH WES control plane with an internal TES backend. A single Go binary acts as API server, workflow runner and task file stager. Each run gets a runner job on Kubernetes; the workflow engine submits individual tasks to Conquest's TES API, and each task stages its inputs from and outputs to S3-compatible object storage. PostgreSQL is the system of record.
audience: Researchers running Nextflow, WDL or Snakemake workflows
features: GA4GH WES v1.1 API
Nextflow, WDL (miniwdl) and Snakemake engines, version selectable per run
Per-task CPU, memory and disk control with platform floors and ceilings
S3/MinIO object storage as the data plane
Helm chart for Kubernetes

products.name: TES Dashboard
products.tagline: Monitor and manage federated TES instances
products.blurb: A dashboard for monitoring TES gateways and nodes, submitting tasks and workflows, and administering a federated TES network.
products.description: The TES Dashboard monitors and manages GA4GH TES instances and workflow execution across federated cloud infrastructure. It shows the health of the gateway and each node, a network map of TES instances, and lets users submit and follow tasks and CWL, Nextflow or Snakemake workflows. Admin tools cover node management and the proTES middleware pipeline.
audience: Operators of a federated TES network
features: Real-time service status of the gateway and federated nodes
Interactive network map of TES instances
Task and workflow submission and tracking (CWL, Nextflow, Snakemake)
Node, instance and middleware management for admins

products.name: GA4GH I/O Schema
products.tagline: A JSON Schema profile for workflow inputs and outputs
products.blurb: An incubating GA4GH JSON Schema profile that gives workflows and tools a machine-readable input/output contract, with a Python validator.
products.description: The GA4GH I/O Schema profile proposes a strict, machine-readable contract for workflow and tool parameters that sits above workflow languages such as CWL, WDL and Nextflow. Generic WES clients can use it to generate input forms and validate complex inputs, such as sample tables, on the client, and AI agents can use it to build valid execution requests. The repository ships the meta-schema and a validation CLI (deliverable D4.3).
audience: Developers of WES clients and registries
features: Meta-schema based on JSON Schema Draft 2020-12
UI widget vocabulary for generated forms
ga4gh-io-schema-validator command-line tool
Planned as an IO_SCHEMA file type for TRS
